# Bayesian Extrapolation of Treatment Effects

[![R Package
Build](https://github.com/TristanFauvel/BExTE/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/TristanFauvel/BExTE/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/TristanFauvel/BExTE/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yml/badge.svg)](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/)
[![License: GPL
v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/LICENSE)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.0.2-blue.svg)](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/DESCRIPTION)
[![R \>=
3.5.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/R-%3E%3D3.5.0-276DC3.svg)](https://www.r-project.org/)

A collection of R tools to :

- Study frequentist and Bayesian operating characteristics of clinical
  trial designs leveraging Bayesian partial extrapolation (also known as
  borrowing).
- Analyze clinical trial data using Bayesian partial extrapolation
  methods.

[](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/articles/index.md)

##### 📚 Vignettes

Step-by-step guides to simulation studies, data generation, borrowing
methods, and case-study replications.

[](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/index.md)

##### 🔧 API reference

Every exported function and R6 class, grouped by topic: data, methods,
plots, tables, operating characteristics.

[](https://github.com/TristanFauvel/BExTE-app)

##### 🖥️ Browser app

Configure, run, and analyze a simulation study from BExTE-app, a
separate Shiny app, without hand-editing config files.

[](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/news/index.md)

## Quick start

### Installation

BExTE needs R \>= 4.0 and, for the MCMC-based methods, a C++ toolchain
and a CmdStan installation - the Stan models are compiled to native
binaries the first time they are used. `install.R` handles all three.

Download `BExTE_0.0.2.tar.gz` and `install.R` from the latest release
into the same directory, then run:

    Rscript install.R

That installs the dependencies, BExTE itself, and CmdStan if it is
missing. Load the package with:

``` r

library(BExTE)
```

Installing by hand

`cmdstanr` is not on CRAN, so its repository has to be declared before
the dependencies will resolve:

``` r

options(repos = c(
  CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org",
  stan = "https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev"
))
install.packages("/path/to/BExTE_0.0.2.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
cmdstanr::check_cmdstan_toolchain(fix = TRUE)
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
```

Working from a source checkout

`renv.lock` pins every dependency. From the checkout:

``` r

renv::restore()
devtools::load_all()
```

### Running and analyzing simulations

- To launch a simulation study, run main.R

- To plot the results of the simulation study, run plots.R

- To create the results tables, run tables.R

### Browser-based interface

Instead of hand-editing config files and running the scripts above, you
can configure, run, and analyze a simulation study from a browser with
[BExTE-app](https://github.com/TristanFauvel/BExTE-app), a Shiny app
built on this package:

``` r

remotes::install_github("TristanFauvel/BExTE-app")
BExTEapp::run_bexte_app()
```

## Design logic

There are three main objects in the simulation framework: source data,
target data, and models. Source data are defined based on the case study
configuration. Target data depend on the source data, and the specific
scenario (drift, sample size). Models correspond to specific methods,
and depend on the source data. They implement methods to estimate their
operating characteristics. The target data objects implement a sample
method, allowing to sample many replicates of the target study.

## Access documentation

The full documentation website is available at
[tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/).

To access it locally instead : browseURL(“docs/index.html”)

## Methods and configurations requiring MCMC inference

MCMC inference with Stan is used in the following scenarios :

- RMP x aprepitant
- separate x aprepitant
- pooling x aprepitant
- conditional_power_prior x aprepitant

When using MCMC inference, the method inherits from the MCMCModel class.
The initialize() method contains a string with the Stan code. This code
is saved in a temporary Stan file which is used to compile the model
(using `self$stan_model <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model(stan_file_path)`). At
inference

### Comparison with existing packages

- psborrow2 implements Bayesian dynamic borrowing in scenarios where a
  two-arm RCT is supplemented with external data on the control arm.

- RBEsT focuses on meta-analytic and mixture models

## Contributing

New contributors are always welcome. Please have a look at the
[contribution
guidelines](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/CONTRIBUTING.md) on
how to get started and to make sure your code complies with our
guidelines.

## Rationale of the design

The core of the code implements the inference logic: a source data class
represents source data, which are observed. Target data are represented
in a different class. They different as we can sample target data
replicates. When initializing a model, source data are provided to it,
as well as methods parameters and MCMC configuration (if applicable), so
as to define a prior. Inference is performed by using the inference
method on target data, which updates properties of the model object with
moments of the treatment effect posterior distribution and, if
applicable, computes the posterior distribution of borrowing parameters.
Note that inference proceeds in two steps: first, if the method uses
empirical Bayes, prior parameters are updated based on the target data
sample, second Bayes” rule is applied.

When launching a simulation study, all scenarios are generated based on
the provided configuration files. These scenarios are then sequentially
treated: source data and target data are initiated, and a model is
defined. Target data replicates are then generated depending on the
target data characteristics. The model is then fitted on each data
replicate, and the corresponding inference metrics and frequentist
metrics are computed. The data from the simulation are then analyzed:
the sweet spot is computed for each metric of interest, and the Bayesian
operating characteristics are estimated.

# Package index

## Data generation

- [`sample_aggregate_binary_data()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sample_aggregate_binary_data.md)
  : Sample aggregate binary data based on the rate and sample size
- [`sample_aggregate_normal_data()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sample_aggregate_normal_data.md)
  : Sample aggregate normal data based on the mean and variance
- [`sample_log_odds_ratios()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sample_log_odds_ratios.md)
  : Sample log odds ratios based on the number of participants and
  responders in each arm
- [`compute_ORs()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/compute_ORs.md)
  : Compute odds ratios based on the number of participants and
  responders in each arm
- [`compute_log_odds_ratio_from_counts()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/compute_log_odds_ratio_from_counts.md)
  : Compute the log odds ratio from count data
- [`rate_from_drift_logOR()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/rate_from_drift_logOR.md)
  : Calculate the success rate in the target study arm from the drift on
  the log odds ratio scale
- [`rate_from_drift_logRR()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/rate_from_drift_logRR.md)
  : Calculate the rate in the target study arm from the drift on the log
  relative risk scale
- [`standard_error_log_odds_ratio()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/standard_error_log_odds_ratio.md)
  : Compute the standard error of the log odds ratio

## Binomial quadrature

Exact posteriors of a difference in response rates for the binomial
borrowing models, computed on a grid instead of sampled

- [`binomial_power_prior_posterior()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/binomial_power_prior_posterior.md)
  : Posterior of the treatment effect under the binomial power prior
- [`binomial_effect_grid()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/binomial_effect_grid.md)
  : Grid of treatment effects covering a binomial posterior
- [`beta_quadrature_nodes()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/beta_quadrature_nodes.md)
  : Quantile midpoints of a Beta distribution
- [`beta_sd()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/beta_sd.md)
  : Standard deviation of a Beta distribution
- [`grid_posterior()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/grid_posterior.md)
  : Summarise a density tabulated on a grid
- [`grid_posterior_cdf()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/grid_posterior_cdf.md)
  : Distribution function of a grid posterior
- [`grid_posterior_pdf()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/grid_posterior_pdf.md)
  : Density of a grid posterior
- [`grid_posterior_quantile()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/grid_posterior_quantile.md)
  : Quantiles of a grid posterior
- [`grid_posterior_sample()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/grid_posterior_sample.md)
  : Draw from a grid posterior

## Vectorised inference

Conjugate updates and frequentist tests evaluated across all replicates
of a scenario at once

- [`normal_mixture_posterior()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/normal_mixture_posterior.md)
  : Conjugate update of a normal mixture prior across replicates
- [`analyse_in_replicate_chunks()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/analyse_in_replicate_chunks.md)
  : Run a vectorised analysis of the replicates in chunks
- [`combine_replicate_results()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/combine_replicate_results.md)
  : Concatenate the results of consecutive chunks of replicates
- [`fit_egidi_mixture()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/fit_egidi_mixture.md)
  : Fit the Egidi, Pauli and Torelli empirical mixture prior
- [`normal_mixture_summary()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/normal_mixture_summary.md)
  : Mean, standard deviation and quantiles of a normal mixture, per
  replicate
- [`normal_mixture_elir_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/normal_mixture_elir_ess.md)
  : ELIR effective sample size of a normal mixture, per replicate
- [`npp_prior_mixture()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/npp_prior_mixture.md)
  : Discretise the normalised power prior as a normal mixture
- [`calibrate_npp_kl()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/calibrate_npp_kl.md)
  : Calibrate the normalised power prior by a KL criterion
- [`summary_t_test_p_value()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/summary_t_test_p_value.md)
  : Two-sample t-test from summary statistics, across replicates

## Operating characteristics

- [`average_power()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/average_power.md)
  : Calculate the average power
- [`average_tie()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/average_tie.md)
  : Calculate the average type 1 error
- [`sweet_spot()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sweet_spot.md)
  : Calculate Sweet Spots for Multiple Metrics
- [`sweet_spot_determination()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sweet_spot_determination.md)
  : Determine Sweet Spot Bounds and Width
- [`upper_bound_proba_FP_MC()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/upper_bound_proba_FP_MC.md)
  : Calculate the upper bound probability of false positive
- [`compute_freq_power()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/compute_freq_power.md)
  : Compute the frequentist power
- [`preposterior_proba_FP_MC()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/preposterior_proba_FP_MC.md)
  : Calculate the probability of false positive
- [`preposterior_proba_TP_MC()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/preposterior_proba_TP_MC.md)
  : Calculate the probability of true positive
- [`prior_moment_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/prior_moment_ess.md)
  : Calculate the prior moment-based Effective Sample Size (ESS) for a
  Bayesian model.
- [`prior_precision_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/prior_precision_ess.md)
  : Calculate the prior precision-based Effective Sample Size (ESS) for
  a Bayesian model.
- [`gaussian_mix_moment_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/gaussian_mix_moment_ess.md)
  : Calculate the moment-based Effective Sample Size (ESS) for a
  Gaussian mixture.
- [`gaussian_mix_precision_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/gaussian_mix_precision_ess.md)
  : Calculate the precision-based Effective Sample Size (ESS) for a
  Gaussian mixture.
- [`compute_freq_power_pooling()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/compute_freq_power_pooling.md)
  : Compute the frequentist power
- [`prior_ess_elir()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/prior_ess_elir.md)
  : Calculate the priorEffective Sample Size (ESS) based on ELIR for a
  Bayesian model.
- [`normal_reference_ess()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/normal_reference_ess.md)
  : Effective sample sizes of a posterior summarised against a normal
  reference
- [`adaptive_power_prior_type_I_error()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/adaptive_power_prior_type_I_error.md)
  : Type I error of the adaptive power prior, computed exactly
- [`log_grid_interpolation()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/log_grid_interpolation.md)
  : Interpolate an expensive function of a positive scalar
- [`interval_score()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/interval_score.md)
  : Interval score of a credible interval
- [`compute_power_with_tie_ci()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/compute_power_with_tie_ci.md)
  : Compute the frequentist power at an estimated type I error

## Monte Carlo uncertainty

Propagating simulation error into the comparison with the frequentist
benchmark at equivalent type I error

- [`binomial_replicate_count()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/binomial_replicate_count.md)
  : Recover the number of Monte Carlo replicates behind a binomial
  estimate
- [`sample_binomial_proportion()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/sample_binomial_proportion.md)
  : Draw from the posterior of a binomial proportion
- [`mover_difference_ci()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/mover_difference_ci.md)
  : Confidence interval for a difference, by variance estimate recovery
- [`add_power_difference_columns()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/add_power_difference_columns.md)
  : Replace success probabilities by power differences
- [`flag_power_differences()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/flag_power_differences.md)
  : Flag power gains and power losses against the comparator

- [`check_colnames()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/check_colnames.md)

  : Append a parameter string to a figure or table filename

  : Function to convert parameters in dataframe to string
- [`hellinger_distance()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/hellinger_distance.md)
  : Compute the Hellinger distance between two normal distributions.
- [`important_drift_values()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/important_drift_values.md)
  : Get important drift values for a given source treatment effect and
  case study configuration.
- [`make_labels_from_parameters()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/make_labels_from_parameters.md)
  : Function to make labels from parameters. Return a label formatted in
  Tex, for example "\$\xi\_\gamma\$ = 0.5, \$\sigma\_\gamma\$ = 0.1"
- [`negative_binomial_regression()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/negative_binomial_regression.md)
  : Estimate rate and standard error
- [`findCalibrationParameter()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/findCalibrationParameter.md)
  : Find Calibration Parameter
- [`get_parameters()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/get_parameters.md)
  : Function to return a dataframe of parameters from json strings
- [`remove_columns_from_df()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/remove_columns_from_df.md)
  : Remove columns from a dataframe
- [`generate_comparison_table()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/generate_comparison_table.md)
  : Generate a comparison table
- [`read_function_code()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/read_function_code.md)
  : Print a function's source code
- [`format_simulation_output_table()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/format_simulation_output_table.md)
  : Format simulation output as a printable table
- [`format_case_study_config()`](https://tristanfauvel.github.io/BExTE/reference/format_case_study_config.md)
  : Format a case study configuration as a printable table
